newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sentiment, CPI spur Belgian bonds to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Sentiment, CPI spur Belgian bonds to higher close.

text.p: Rampant bullish sentiment, unleashed by well-received U.S. inflation data, pushed Belgian linear bonds sharply higher on Tuesday, but traders said they felt to move may have been slightly overdone.
"The market is very, very bullish. But I don't know if it will carry on up or not," one trader said.
"It was reasonably busy today, but once again there were very few domestic investors," he added.
The yield of the benchmark 2007 OLO dropped below the key six percent level to 5.94 percent from Monday's closing 6.06, and the spread over Bunds widened to 12 basis points from 11.
Traders said the 12 basis points drop in the benchmark yield may also have been a touch overdone.
"I feel it went too fast. I think it might rise again," one trader said.
The afternoon surge, following a cautiously higher morning, followed U.S. consumer price index figures for March showing a lower-than-expected 0.1 percent rise.
Traders welcomed this as a sign that the U.S. Federal Reserve might not be pushed after all to raise interest rates again in May.
However, the rally was as unexpected as it was sharp.
"One indication of that was the low OLO exchange auction," one trader said.

The auction, in which the Treasury offered OLO lines 13 (7.00 pct April 1999), 25 (5.00 pct March 2001), 6 (9.00 pct March 2003), 19 (6.50 pct March 2005) and 26 (6.25 pct March 2007) in exchange for OLO 4 (9.25 pct Jan 1998), raised only 14.7 billion francs.
"It was low because no one expected the market rally," a trader said.
